The generator script IS the map: `tileAt({ x, y, world })` evaluates deterministically on every side, like heightAt/materialAt. Infinite by default: omit width/height and tileAt is sampled over a streamed window that follows the players forever, exactly like heightmap terrain. Cells read like an image grid: x → +X, row 0 at the TOP (2d-top: y → +Z down-screen; 2d-side: y → −Y downward), so level data reads top-to-bottom like ASCII art in both modes. Gameplay mutation is sparse and a cell is a dot: ctx.place.tiles[x][y] reads override ?? tileAt; = id paints one cell, = 0 carves it to empty, delete returns it to the generator. | { kind: "off"; decorations?: DecorationDef } // Terrain disabled - no terrain rendering. `decorations` still dresses the place's mesh floors: a scatter bed with `surface: { mesh }` draws as the layer `scatter:<bed id>` of this config, so an authored layer of that id is the bed's look (`material`), its reach (`maxDistance`) and its items: the same words a heightmap's cover takes. // TerrainDef, kind "heightmap" seed?: number // Seed for deterministic generation: a number, like every other seed in the spec. (Legacy docs may carry a string; the engine hashes String(seed), so both parse and generate identically.) materials?: Array<{ id: string; albedo?: string; pbr?: boolean | "fal1"; tint?: number | string; normal?: string; roughness?: string; textureScale?: number; metalness?: number; normalStrength?: number; roughnessIntensity?: number; antiTiling?: "none" | "stochastic"; filter?: "pixel" | "linear"; macro?: { scale?: number; hue?: number; value?: number } }> // [{ id, albedo: "cdn/x.png", pbr: true (the textured default: the engine cooks its normal, roughness and height; a picture carves its seams by its own grain with or without pbr; a weight ramp over metres of noise is the soft edge), tint? (alone = flat color, meeting other tints by dither), textureScale? meters per tile, macro? { scale m, hue °, value }: the slow world-space drift of the shown colour (default { scale: 20, hue: 10, value: 0.12 }; { hue: 0, value: 0 } = none), the ground cover wears it too }]; a point keeps its three heaviest; steep ground (from about 37°) projects the picture from the side by itself; live: ctx.place.terrain.materials.<id> = {…} (delete removes) generator?: ScriptRef // scripts/<file>.js exporting heightAt(ctx) → meters and materialAt(ctx) → { <materialId>: weight } (the engine normalizes the weights). One ctx object: { x, z, place, noise, seedOffset(n), metersPerTile } in world meters: noise is builtin/noise's functions, seedOffset(n) decorrelates each layer under the authored seed; materialAt's ctx adds worldHeight, height01 (the place in verticalRange), slope (1 − normal.y: 0 flat, 1 vertical, 0.29 = 45°), normal and neighbor(ox, oz) → { worldHeight, height01, slope } | null off the chunk. An optional paintOffsetAt(ctx) → { x, z } meters (heightAt's ctx) moves where the painted terrain:material fields and the natural mask are read, held within 2 m; readField reads the cells as painted. heightAt runs ~17k times per 80 m chunk across its detail levels: a per-call loop over a point list is the whole cost of the world; a track or river is a mark (heightmap-terrain skill) verticalRange?: { min: number; max: number } // { min, max } meters, default { min: -32, max: 256 }: the band height01 and the height tints normalize over (and the skirt's depth); the ground is built at whatever heightAt returns, inside the band or not, and the engine says so once when it leaves: set it to the real span so height01 reads 0..1 marks?: HeightmapTerrainMarkMap // { <key>: HeightmapTerrainMark }: a strip (`path`, `road`, `river`: `points: [x, z][]`, `width`), a disc (`lake`: `at`, `radius`), an area (`flatten`, `clear-scatter`: `center` + `shape`, or spelled as a strip `{ points, width }`), an outline (`hole`: `points: [x, z][]`, three or more, closed), a shore (`sea`: `level`). Marks carve in the order flatten → sea → lake → river → path → road → clear-scatter → hole, each seeing the last kind's result; overlapping waters merge low and never dam; a mark overrides the generator in its area: edit the mark, heightAt does nothing there; a `hole` removes the ground inside its outline (not drawn, no collider, no cover: a tunnel mouth, a shaft; the tunnel itself is your geometry) and moves no height; `spawn api HeightmapTerrainMark <kind>` prints each kind's fields and its defaults; live: ctx.place.terrain.marks.<key> = {…} (a standing key merges; `delete` removes); a painted stroke stays over the new ground decorations?: DecorationDef // ground cover (heightmap-terrain skill) water?: LiquidSpec | Array<{ id?: string } & LiquidSpec> // the liquid every `terrain:water` sheet of this place wears: a lake mark's `liquid` shape, `material` included; omitted: the engine's still pond. A list holds several liquids at once, one per entry, each worn by its own field's sheets: `terrain:water:<id>` for an entry with an `id`, `terrain:water` for the one entry without material?: ScriptedMaterialSpec // Scripted material for the ground: the same `{ kind: "scripted", script, params }` contract objects and tile ground use (spawn api builtin/three for the ctx), worn by the whole ground, near and far. The ground is one mesh at the world origin: `positionWorld` and `positionLocal` are the world position, `uv()` is the world x, z in metres, and `vertexColor()` is the ground's own colour (the `materials` as `materialAt` weights them, a textured one at its average colour). A material with no colorNode wears that colour under its own shading. The `materials`' pictures, taken from the side on steep ground, reach it only through `ctx.terrain.ground`. The shape stays `heightAt`'s: the material shades the ground and does not move it. A broken script keeps the plain ground until the next edit. // TerrainDef, kind "voxel" cellSize?: number // World metres per voxel cell (default 1): 0.125 | 0.25 | 0.5 | 1 | 2. A 3D place takes each and its chunk follows the cell; a 2D place takes 0.5, 1, 2. A write of any other value is refused. Terraria-style 2D dig games read best at 0.5 (a ~1.8 m character stands 3-4 cells tall). Cell-addressed APIs keep integer CELL coordinates; world position = cell × cellSize. `materialAt(ctx)` still receives world metres. defaultSlices?: { // The gameplay slice for 2D place modes (defaults to the terrain origin). The slice contract: in a 2D place this single cell layer is what renders, what edits target, AND what physics collides/samples: colliders are merged rects of the slice's solid cells, built locally on every machine, and solidity reads use the slice cell, never a player's preserved-axis depth. topY?: number // 2d-top: world Y of the played cell layer. sideZ?: number // 2d-side: world Z of the played cell layer. } materials?: Record<string, VoxelMaterialDef> // { <id>: VoxelMaterialDef }; live: ctx.place.terrain.materials.<id> = {…} (delete removes) generator?: ScriptRef // Generator script reference (exports materialAt) marks?: VoxelTerrainMarkMap // Voxel terrain marks for flattening pads, carving ponds/rivers, repainting paths, clearing airspace, and stamping one-off voxel structures. meshing?: { style?: "blocky" | "smooth" } // `"smooth"` draws the ground rounded over its cells; digging and reads stay on the cells, within half a cell of the drawn surface. decorations?: DecorationDef // ground cover: the same layers as a heightmap's, grown on the top face of every block that counts as terrain surface, caves included; bindings by material id (voxel-terrain skill) // TerrainDef, kind "3d-rooms" wallThickness?: number // Wall thickness in meters (default: tileSize * 0.2). // TerrainDef, kind "tilemap" tileSize?: number // World units per (square) cell. Default 1. width?: number // Optional map bounds in cells: author BOTH for a bounded map (tileAt sampled inside the rect, empty outside, the whole map centered on the place origin), omit BOTH for an infinite map (tileAt sampled for any integer cell and streamed in a window around the players, cell (0, 0) anchored at the world origin: generator coords = floor(world / tileSize)). tileset: string // Tileset atlas texture URL; a plain tileable texture is one tile only with `tilesetColumns: 1` (default 4 columns). tilesetColumns?: number // Atlas grid width in tiles (default 4); rows derived from the image. tilesetFrames?: number // Animation frames stacked in the tileset image as whole-atlas row groups below frame 0 (frame-major vertical concat), 2–16. Declared, never inferred: omit for a static tileset; extra rows WITHOUT this field are spatial variants (random-per-cell, picked by tileAt ids), not animation. Playback is loop-only at `tilesetFps` and costs nothing per tick (a shader V-shift); lit tilesets animate their normal atlas in lockstep automatically. tilesetFps?: number // Playback rate in frames per second (default 12); plays only when `tilesetFrames` is set. generator?: ScriptRef // Generator script reference (exports tileAt({ x, y, world }) => tile id; 0/null = empty). `world.state` is the room's ctx.world.state, read-only; when a key tileAt read changes, the map is asked again. solidTiles?: number[] // Tile ids that compose merged static colliders in 2D places. material?: ScriptedMaterialSpec // Scripted material for the tile surface: the same `{ kind: "scripted", script, params }` contract objects use (spawn api builtin/three for the ctx). Inside `material(ctx)`, `ctx.tile` carries the per-cell inputs: `id` (the tile id tileAt returned), `uv` (0..1 across the cell), and `uvRect` (the default atlas rect for that id). Compute exact UVs for any sheet layout (margins, spacing, multiple tilesets by id range), and animate tiles by deriving the sampled cell from `time`: water/lava frames play in-shader with zero per-tick cost. The engine keeps placement, chunking, and batching; tiles render double-sided, and opaque materials keep the standard 0.5 alpha cutout. A broken script falls back to the plain `tileset` grid until the next edit. // TerrainDef, kind "off" decorations?: DecorationDef // Ground cover over the place's mesh floors: the layers a mesh-surface scatter bed draws with (`scatter:<bed id>`), spelled as a heightmap's `decorations`.
